fluff.overview:
One of the most popular Star League BattleMechs, many Highlanders accompanied General Aleksandr Kerensky into exile during the Exodus. Some were mothballed, but many found their way into the toumans of the Clans. As Clan technology advanced over the subsequent centuries, weapons systems were progressively upgraded until the design known as the Highlander IIC finally emerged around 2858 during the Golden Century. By the Civil War era, though no new Highlander IICs had been produced since the thirtieth century, several hundred remained in scattered use throughout the touman of every Clan.

The Jihad and subsequent conflicts revitalized production. Clan Wolf established refit facilities on Weingarten to convert salvaged Inner Sphere Highlander chassis into IIC-standard machines, an operation that continued for seventy years. When Clan Hell's Horses captured Weingarten in 3142, they discovered the intact refit line and further enhanced it to produce entirely new Highlander IIC variants, demonstrating the enduring appeal of this venerable assault design.
fluff.capabilities:
The Highlander IIC retains the fundamental design philosophy of its Inner Sphere ancestor while dramatically upgrading its combat potential through Clan technology. The primary armament centers on an EMRG "Captain" Series Gauss rifle and a Type XXVI "Great Bow" LRM-20 launcher for devastating long-range engagements. At closer distances, a pair of MPA-14 Mod. 12a Streak SRM-6 launchers ensure that every missile finds its target, while three Series PPS-VIII Medium Pulse Lasers provide accurate close-range fire. With the use of newer, lighter Clan weapons, the damage potential of the Highlander has roughly doubled compared to the original design.

Fourteen and a half tons of Arcadia Compound Delta VII ferro-fibrous armor represent the maximum protection that can be crammed onto the frame, making the IIC exceptionally durable in prolonged engagements. Twelve double heat sinks manage thermal output adequately, though aggressive alphas can still tax the cooling system. The retention of three Prentiss-IIIA jump jets preserves the hallmark ninety-meter jumping capability, allowing Clan MechWarriors to execute the infamous Highlander Burial just as effectively as their Inner Sphere predecessors. The generous ammunition supply means the IIC rarely needs to conserve rounds even during extended Trials.
fluff.history:
The Highlander IIC traces its origins to the Golden Century, when Clan scientists methodically upgraded the surviving Highlander chassis brought on the Exodus with progressively more advanced Clan technology. The Arcadia BattleMech Plant CM-T15, operated by Clan Star Adder on Arcadia in the Rechlan system, served as the primary production facility, and the design saw widespread adoption across nearly every Clan touman. Production eventually tapered off, and by the thirty-first century no new Highlander IICs had been built for over a hundred years, though hundreds remained in scattered service.

The Word of Blake Jihad prompted Clan Wolf to revive the design through an innovative approach. Operating out of an extensive boneyard on Weingarten, the Wolves established the W-7 Facilities refit line to convert purchased, scavenged, or salvaged Inner Sphere Highlander chassis into updated Clan-specification IICs. This operation sustained Wolf production for seventy years, during which new combat variants including the IIC 2 and IIC 3 were developed to address evolving battlefield requirements.

When Clan Wolf abandoned Weingarten during the Dark Age upheavals, Clan Hell's Horses occupied the planet in 3142 and discovered the intact W-7 refit facilities. However, the post-Blackout hunger for military hardware had dried up all sources of spare Inner Sphere Highlander chassis. Undaunted, the Horses enhanced the production line to build the required SL-XT chassis on-site, sourcing parts from their facilities on New Oslo and the Clan Sea Fox line on Alnabog. The resulting Highlander IIC 4 proved a formidable weapon during Operation Noyan, demonstrating that the ancient assault design still had much to offer on the modern battlefield.
fluff.deployment: Introduced in 3072 during the Jihad, the Highlander IIC 2 is configured as an all-range combatant with enhanced anti-infantry capability. The LRM-20 is replaced with three ATM 6 launchers providing flexible ammunition options, while the Medium Pulse Lasers give way to ER Medium Lasers for extended range. Most particularly, six AP Gauss Rifles fitted into the left arm give the variant devastating anti-infantry firepower. An endo steel chassis replaces the original internal structure, allowing a slight increase in armor protection while accommodating the expanded weapons suite.
